public_rationale: The ordinary task-level reading is contradicted by deployed customer-service automation. Intercom reported resolved customer questions in April 2024 and described Fin generating answers directly in June. A customer challenged false-positive resolutions, which supports the surrounding concern about reliability. It does not establish that the system automated nothing. The evidence supports some working automation, not universal reliability.
limitations: A definition requiring complete workflows or perfect reliability would change the assessment, but the speaker supplied neither requirement.

statement.excerpt: Even though it doesn't really automate anything.
statement.document_title: Rot Economics - An Interview With MIT's Daron Acemoglu

our_interpretation: 'It' refers to generative AI in the surrounding exchange.
The ordinary reading is that generative AI was not actually completing real work tasks without human execution of each task.
Answering customer questions can constitute automation even when people handle exceptions. 'Really' does not specify an error-free or whole-job requirement.
For this ongoing observation, use April–June 2024, the latest complete quarter before publication.
criteria.support_condition: Representative deployment evidence establishes that apparent automation still required humans to execute the tasks, with no credible successful counterexample.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented deployment in the target period uses generative AI to complete a real task without a person executing each instance.
